parts.title: My first fossil
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When I was eight, my grandfather took me to a beach in the south of England, where he had found fossils as a boy. "Look carefully at the stones," he said. "Sometimes, an animal that lived millions of years ago is hiding in one of them."

I spent two hours walking along the beach with my head down. I found shells, old glass and a lot of grey pebbles, but nothing special. I was about to give up when something shiny caught my eye. It was a round stone with a beautiful spiral pattern on it.

"That is an ammonite," my grandfather said with a big smile. "It is about a hundred and fifty million years old." I could not believe that I was holding something that old. It was no bigger than my hand, but it felt like treasure.

I kept the fossil on my desk for years. Now, I am studying geology at university, and my grandfather is very proud. Last week, I gave him a gift: a small box with a new ammonite inside. He put it on the shelf next to his old photographs.

parts.title: The king of the dinosaurs
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Tyrannosaurus rex, often called T. rex, is probably the most famous dinosaur of all. [1] It lived about sixty-seven million years ago, in the area that is now North America.

T. rex was about twelve metres long and as heavy as an African elephant. [2] Its head alone was over a metre and a half long, and its teeth were as long as bananas.

For a long time, people thought that T. rex was a slow animal. [3] Scientists now believe that it could probably walk quickly but could not run very fast.

The arms of T. rex were very short, and they could not even reach its mouth. [4] They were strong, however, and may have helped the animal to hold its food.

The first almost complete skeleton was found in 1902. [5] Today, you can see a copy of it in museums all over the world.
sentences: This is why children everywhere love to draw and read about it.
Its bones were found in rocks in places such as Canada and the United States.
It had a huge head with a very powerful bite.
New studies show that this idea may not be correct.
For many years, scientists did not know what they were for.
It was sold to a museum for a large amount of money.

gaps.explanation: The sentence about bones found in Canada and the United States follows the place where it lived.
A huge head with a powerful bite follows the animal's size, and the next sentence gives the head's length.
New studies show the idea of a slow animal may be wrong, so scientists now believe it could walk quickly.
Scientists did not know what the short arms were for, and the next sentence says they were strong.
The skeleton sold to a museum explains why a copy can be seen in museums today.

parts.title: Why did the dinosaurs disappear?
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: About sixty-six million years ago, something terrible happened to the Earth. A giant rock from space, [1] than ten kilometres wide, hit the ocean near Mexico. The hit sent so [2] dust and smoke into the air that the sky went dark. Plants could not grow in the cold and dark, and animals [3] ate the plants soon had no food. Slowly, most of the big dinosaurs died out. However, some small dinosaurs [4] able to survive, and we know them today as birds. [5] you look at a bird in your garden, you are looking at a very distant relative of T. rex. It is a surprising thought, [6] it is true.

gaps.explanation: More than ten kilometres: comparative form for size.
So much dust and smoke: an uncountable quantity.
Animals that ate the plants: a relative pronoun.
Some small dinosaurs were able to survive: plural past.
If you look at a bird: a condition for the idea.
It is a surprising thought, but it is true: contrast.

parts.title: A talk about fossils
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: marguerite
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to our fossil workshop. A fossil is the remains of a plant or an animal that lived a very long time ago. Most fossils are found in a kind of rock called limestone. When an animal died, its body was sometimes covered by mud, and over millions of years, the mud became hard stone. The soft parts of the animal, such as the skin, usually disappeared, but the bones and the shells stayed. This is why most fossils that we find are teeth, bones and shells. The biggest fossil ever discovered was a plant, a tree that was over thirty metres tall. Some fossils are very small, and you need a microscope to see them. To find fossils, the best places are beaches with high cliffs, because the sea washes the rocks away and shows what is inside. Always wear a hard hat there, and never dig at the bottom of a cliff. Remember to bring a notebook so that you can write down where you found each fossil.

gaps.prompt: Most fossils are found in a rock called ___
gaps.explanation: A kind of rock called limestone.

The soft parts, such as the skin, usually disappeared.
The biggest fossil ever discovered was a plant, a tree.

gaps.prompt: Visitors should wear a hard ___ near cliffs
gaps.explanation: Always wear a hard hat there.

gaps.prompt: Write down where you found each fossil in a ___

parts.title: An interview with a fossil collector
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Atticus, you have a famous collection of fossils. How did it begin?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: When I was ten, I found a small shell fossil on a school trip. My teacher said it was a million years old, and from that day I was hooked.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How many fossils do you have now?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: More than three thousand. Most of them are in boxes in my garage, but the best ones are in the glass cases in my living room.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Which one is your favourite?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: A tiny fish, only the size of my thumb. You can see every bone, even the eyes. It was found in a quarry in Germany.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Have you ever been in danger?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Once. I was digging below a cliff when a large rock fell next to me. Luckily, I was wearing a helmet. Since then, I have always worked with a friend.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you ever sell fossils?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Never. I think they belong to everyone. I lend many of them to schools, so that children can touch them.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice do you have for beginners?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Start in your own area. Ask at the local museum where people find fossils, and join a club. You will learn faster with other people.
